pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Read max advertising data length from the controller
pr_body:
Read maximum advertising data length from the controller at host initialization and store the returned value. 
Add a test that check that we get the right error code when trying to set too large advertising data and that we are able to send/receive large advertising data.

Fix https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45230

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: Read maximum advertising data length
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The host is now capable of segmenting and sending up to 1650 octets for extended advertising, but the controller may not support such large values (based on `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ADV_DATA_LEN_MAX`). 

The host should read the maximum adverting data length and reject requests for values larger than the response when the application requests it. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
On host init do a call to send the `bt_hci_rp_le_read_max_adv_data_len` request to the controller and store the result, as we do for e.g. ACL and ISO buffer sizes, and rejects requests to `bt_le_ext_adv_set_data` and `bt_le_per_adv_set_data` with too large advertising data. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
N/A
comments: I guess we can set a low priority on this? We can rely on the controller returning an error code when setting too much data

> I guess we can set a low priority on this? We can rely on the controller returning an error code when setting too much data

Aren't priorities for bugs only? 

Should we expect the controller to do the checks if `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_PARAM_CHECK=n`?

> 

Good point. I was not aware of this configuration, and I see it is specific to BT_LL_SW_SPLIT. Disabling this configuration puts the controller in a non-qualifiable state. In either case it may be a good idea to add this functionality to the host as it improves the debugging experience

review_comments: We should add this error code as a `@retval` entry in the documentation for the public API functions that may call this function

From what I can see the functions doesn't document their return code and simply say "return 0 on success or (negative) error code otherwise". If it's fine for you I'll update the documentation of those functions in a future PR.
I kinda agree with you but at the same time this isn't a "unrecoverable error" right? We should define how we want to use the different log level in the Bluetooth code guidelines
This function and the `bt_dev.le.max_adv_data_len` should be guarded with `CONFIG_BT_BROADCASTER` as we don't use them for e.g. central-only builds

```suggestion
		LOG_ERR("adv or scan rsp data too large (%d > max %d)", total_len_bytes,
```
This is a recoverable error, so based on the logging convention it's preferable to use a warning
